chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man says to his wife,

And we asked him about the Zahaar, when does the expiation fall upon its perpetrator? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he intends to copulate with his wife.' I said: 'If he divorces her before he copulates with her, is there an expiation upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, the expiation has dropped from him.'

I said: 'If he fasts part of it, then falls ill and breaks the fast, does he start again or complete what remains upon him?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he fasts a month and falls ill, he starts again; and if he exceeds the month by one day or two days, he builds upon what remains.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The free woman and the slave woman are equal, except that upon the slave is half of what is upon the free from the expiation, and there is no emancipation upon him nor charity, but rather upon him is the fasting of a month.'
ai.seo_question: When does the expiation for Zahaar become due and how is it calculated for slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanics of Zahaar, establishing that the expiation is triggered by the intent to consummate rather than the act itself, and clarifies that divorce before consummation waives the penalty. It further details the jurisprudential nuances of fulfilling the fasting expiation during illness and distinguishes the slave's obligation as solely fasting, excluding the emancipation required for a free man. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on the precise timing of legal obligations and the proportional nature of duties based on social status.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The man is saying to his wife, ‘You are unto me like the back of’ – either his paternal aunt or his maternal aunt’. Heasws said: ‘It is the Zahaar’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And we asked him about the Zahaar, when does the expiation occur upon its perpetrator?’ So heasws said: ‘When he intends to copulate with his wife’. I said, ‘Supposing he divorces her before he copulates with her, would there be an expiation upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘The expiation does not drop off from him’.

I said, ‘So if he were to Fasts some, so he falls sick, so he breaks the Fasting, shall he start again or he has to complete what remains upon him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he Fasted a month, so he fell sick, he starts again, and if he exceeded upon the month by one day or two days, he builds upon what remains’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The free woman and the owned (slave) woman are equal, apart from that upon the owned is half of what is upon the free, from the expiation, and there is no emancipation upon him nor a charity, but rather upon him is the Fasting for a month’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following:
“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a man says to his wife that she is like the back of his paternal or maternal aunt. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is al-Zihar.’

He (the narrator) has said that we asked him (the Imam) about al-Zihar and about when expiation becomes due on such man. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is when he wants to go to bed with his wife.’ I then asked, ‘Will there be expiation if he divorces her before going to bed with her?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Expiation does not fall off of him.’

I then asked, ‘If he fasts a part of fasting, then he falls ill and he discontinues his fast, must he start it all over again or continue from where he had left to complete what he owes?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has fasted one month, then has fallen ill, he must start all over again, but if he has done more than one month by one day or two days he can continue from there onward to complete the rest.’

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) said, ‘Free and slaves are the same except that slaves owe one-half of expiation on a free person. He (a slave) does not owe setting free of slaves or charity. He must only fast for one month.’”
